scenes.narration: At 3:44 in the morning the bell in my guest room rang, and nobody has stayed there for years.
It is a little brass bell on the bedside table, the kind you tap for service. I bought it as a joke. It had never made a sound without a hand on it.
I walked down the corridor with my phone torch. The door was shut. Under it, a thin line of yellow light, like a lamp that somebody had left on.
I opened the door. The room was dark and cold. The bed was made, flat and tight. And the bell was shaking, slowly, as if the table were breathing.
I asked who was there. The bell rang once. Then twice. Then, very clearly, three times, the way a person rings when they are getting impatient.
I looked at the note beside it. It was my own handwriting. Please ring for anything you need. I had written it years ago, for guests.
The bell rang again. A new line of ink appeared at the bottom of the note while I watched. Room service for the man in the corridor.
I felt the floorboards creak behind me, and a cold finger tapped the bell once, right over my shoulder. Thank you, said a voice. I will take my tea now.
So tell me. Do you make the tea, or lock the door?
